groups.root_cause: An error while inspecting one PR's CI aborts the whole repository poll loop instead of being caught for that PR alone.
The main-red branch returns early, before job logs are fetched, so the ledger signature uses a generic conclusion instead of the real error and runner image.
Job URL validation compares the repository name case-sensitively against the operator-configured spelling.
Rerun resolution doesn't treat a skipped conclusion as a terminal result, so the retry never resolves.
When the rerun POST response is lost, nothing is persisted that would let the poller reconcile the accepted rerun with its later result.
Rerun lookup searches only the newest workflow attempt instead of searching across all attempts for the rerun job.
Main-red notifications are deduplicated per failing check instead of per repository.
Suppressed PRs are only re-inspected when the PR itself changes, not when main goes back to green.
Cancelled matrix legs are treated as rerunnable failures and recorded as flakes, even though fail-fast cancelled them and they never failed.
The rerun cap is used up before the rerun request succeeds, and GitHub's refusal for an in-progress workflow is mishandled as an access error instead of being deferred.
An unreleased new table is altered by a second migration in the same change instead of being defined once.
Rerun reconciliation depends on the single page of 100 GraphQL check contexts, so retried jobs past that page are never seen.
The poller emits failure notifications for closed tracked PRs without running them through the CI classifier.
The feed excerpt is taken from the start of the job log instead of the area around the failure.
The new `[github] ci_reruns` config switch and its enabled default are missing from GUIDE.md.
The signature extractor picks the first log line containing 'fail' or 'error', which is often an echoed input rather than the real failure.
Main-red state is cleared while main's newest commit still has pending checks, instead of being kept until the checks reach a final green result.
